question: What is the minimum attendance requirement to appear for semester end exams?
answer: Students must maintain a minimum of 75% attendance in each registered course. A relaxation up to 65% may be granted by the Dean of Academic Affairs strictly on certified medical grounds.

question: Where can I view my internal assessment marks and CGPA?
answer: Internal assessment marks, mid-term grades, and semester CGPA transcripts can be viewed on the University Student ERP Portal under the 'Academic Records' tab.

question: How do I apply for course re-evaluation or back paper registration?
answer: Re-evaluation applications open within 10 days of result declarations via the Examination Cell window in Block A, Ground Floor, or online through the Examination Portal.

question: How can first-year students join technical and cultural clubs?
answer: Clubs conduct their annual recruitment drive during 'Orientation Week' in August/September. Interested students can register at stalls in the Student Activity Centre (SAC) or fill out online Google forms shared on official social handles.

question: What are the major active societies on campus?
answer: The campus hosts several active bodies including the Coding Club, Robotics Society, Literary & Debating Society, Dramatics Club (Natya), Music Society (Dhwani), and the Photography Club.

question: How do I start a new student club or chapter?
answer: To start a new club, you need a minimum of 15 founding student members and a faculty advisor. Submit a formal charter proposal to the Office of the Dean of Student Affairs in Block C.

question: Where is the Central Library located and what are its borrowing limits?
answer: The Central Library is located in Block B. Undergraduate students can borrow up to 4 books for a duration of 14 days using their Student ID card.

question: What are the library overdue fines and renewal policies?
answer: Overdue fines are charged at ₹5 per day per book. Books can be renewed online once through the Library OPAC portal provided no other student has placed a hold.

question: How do I access IEEE, Springer, and digital journals from off-campus?
answer: Remote access to digital libraries (IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, Springer) is enabled via the University RemoteXs VPN credentials provided during college onboarding.

question: When is the annual cultural fest held and how can I get a pass?
answer: The annual cultural fest 'Utsav' is held in February. Entry passes are issued via digital QR on the college events app using your student roll number.

question: What is the annual technical hackathon and who can participate?
answer: 'InnovateX', the 36-hour inter-college hackathon, takes place every October in the Central Computer Lab. Teams of 2 to 4 undergraduate students can register online.

question: Where are campus event updates and guest lecture schedules published?
answer: All upcoming seminars, workshops, and guest lectures are announced on the Digital Notice Board screens in Block A and on the official University Telegram announcement channel.

question: What are the general university academic hours and office timings?
answer: Regular lectures and laboratory sessions run from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, Monday through Friday. Administrative offices operate from 9:30 AM to 4:30 PM.

question: What are the Central Library and reading room hours?
answer: The Central Library is open from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM on weekdays. The 24/7 air-conditioned Reading Hall in Block B remains accessible all night during semester examination weeks.

question: What are the hostel in-out timings and gate curfew rules?
answer: Hostel gates close at 9:30 PM for all undergraduate resident students. Late entry up to 10:30 PM requires prior digital leave permission from the Hostel Warden.

question: Where is the campus health centre / dispensary located?
answer: The University Health Centre is located near Hostel Block 3. A medical officer and 24/7 emergency ambulance service are available on campus for all enrolled students.

question: What sports facilities and gymnasiums are available on campus?
answer: The Sports Complex features a synthetic running track, basketball and tennis courts, indoor badminton courts, and a gymnasium located opposite the Student Cafeteria.

question: Where are the ATMs and bank branches located on campus?
answer: A nationalized bank branch and 2 ATMs (SBI and HDFC) are located near the Main Security Gate next to the University Post Office.

question: Which coding clubs and developer communities can students join?
answer: Students can join technical student chapters by taking these steps: 1) Explore the 'Clubs & Societies' category to view active tech societies on campus. 2) Attend the annual Club Orientation & Recruitment Drive held at the start of the semester. 3) Join the official campus developer Discord or WhatsApp groups for weekly problem-solving meetups. 4) Participate in beginner workshops, internal hack nights, and peer code reviews hosted by senior student leads.

question: Where can I practice DSA and competitive programming?
answer: Follow this structured step-by-step roadmap: 1) Start on GeeksforGeeks or LeetCode Explore cards to master foundational data structures (Arrays, Strings, Linked Lists, Trees). 2) Practice curated topic-wise problem lists (e.g., Striver's SDE Sheet, NeetCode 150) on LeetCode. 3) Participate in weekly beginner contests on CodeChef or LeetCode to build speed under time constraints. 4) Progress to Codeforces Div. 3/Div. 2 contests for advanced algorithmic problem-solving and competitive rating growth.

question: How do I prepare for campus placements and coding rounds?
answer: Prepare effectively for on-campus drives with this 4-step plan: 1) Master Core CS Fundamentals including Object-Oriented Programming (OOP), DBMS, Operating Systems, and Computer Networks. 2) Solve 150-250 medium-level DSA questions on LeetCode covering dynamic programming, graphs, and trees. 3) Build 2-3 production-grade full-stack or systems projects with live deployments and clear README documentation. 4) Practice timed mock coding tests, quantitative aptitude assessments, and peer mock interviews.

question: Where can I find hackathons and how do I form a team?
answer: Get started with hackathons by following these steps: 1) Discover upcoming national and global hackathons on platforms like Devfolio, Devpost, MLH, and Unstop. 2) Check campus noticeboards and tech club channels for the annual University Hackathon. 3) Form a balanced multidisciplinary team of 3-4 members (frontend designer, backend engineer, and pitch presenter). 4) Prepare project boilerplates and GitHub templates in advance to accelerate prototyping during the event.

question: How do I find internships and build a resume as a first or second year student?
answer: Early-stage students can land internships with this focused approach: 1) Format a clean, single-page ATS-friendly resume highlighting technical skills, GitHub links, and GPA. 2) Build 2 distinct deployed personal projects solving real problems rather than generic tutorial clones. 3) Search for remote internships and student programs on Wellfound (AngelList), LinkedIn, Internshala, and Y Combinator Work at a Startup. 4) Reach out directly to alumni and engineering founders with concise cold emails demonstrating how your skills can contribute.

question: How do I start with open source?
answer: Begin your open-source journey with these actionable milestones: 1) Master Git and GitHub fundamentals (forking, branching, committing, and opening Pull Requests). 2) Filter repositories using 'good first issue' and 'help wanted' labels on GitHub or GoodFirstIssue.dev. 3) Participate in beginner-friendly open-source initiatives like Hacktoberfest and GirlScript Summer of Code (GSSoC). 4) Contribute documentation fixes and unit tests before tackling major features in target Google Summer of Code (GSoC) organizations.

question: Which free resources should I use to learn web development and AI/ML?
answer: Leverage these top free, industry-standard learning tracks: 1) For Web Development: Follow The Odin Project (full-stack JavaScript/Ruby) or freeCodeCamp for interactive coding practice. 2) For Computer Science Foundations: Take Harvard's CS50x on edX for core programming concepts and problem-solving. 3) For AI & Machine Learning: Complete the Practical Deep Learning course on fast.ai and Andrew Ng's Machine Learning specialization materials. 4) For Data Science & ML Practice: Work through Kaggle micro-courses and compete in beginner Kaggle tabular competitions.

question: Are the computer labs open after class hours for project work?
answer: Students can access computer laboratories beyond standard lecture hours with these guidelines: 1) General computing labs in the Main Academic Block remain accessible on weekdays until [8:00 PM] with a valid student ID card. 2) Advanced research and project labs require written permission from the Department Lab In-Charge or Faculty Advisor. 3) High-performance compute servers and GPU workstations can be accessed remotely via university VPN. 4) Check the Central Computer Centre noticeboard for extended opening hours during hackathons and exam weeks.
